# KeyManager v1

<!-- Generated by sdkgen; edit internal/cmd/sdkgen/service_docs.go. -->

Use Gophercloud v2.15.0's keymanager/v1 API through one authenticated service object. Connection manages authentication, region, endpoint interface and TLS.

| Operation | openstacksdk | Go |
|---|---|---|
| Service access | `conn.key_manager` | `conn.KeyManagerV1(ctx)` |
| Optional arguments and defaults | keyword arguments | concrete options and operation-specific `With...Options` |
| Extension inputs | `**attrs`, `**query` | supported `With...Field/Query/Header` options |
| Results | Resource or generator | typed values and errors, or `iter.Seq2` |

Native API coverage and openstacksdk Resource/workflow coverage are tracked separately. Python input aliases are not automatically applied to Go fields. Default responses use Gophercloud models; SDK-owned additions are documented per service. Editing a returned response does not automatically persist it.

`Waits.WaitForStatus/WaitForDelete` waits on concrete Secret/Container/Order/SecretStore targets. See [wait comparison](waits-python.md) for nil status, timing defaults, payload errors and remaining ACL/quota scope, and [SecretStore waits](secret-store-waits-python.md) for flat metadata, defaults and actual responses. Both named wait operations remain unresolved.

`Containers/Orders/Secrets.ListRecords/AllRecords` provides Source fields, function options and marker/offset pagination. See [Barbican record lists](record-lists-python.md) for wire queries, local filters and response evidence.

Key-manager mutation and wait mappings are described in [Python Proxy comparison](python-parity.md).

`Orders.Resources.List/All` classifies `resource.WithFilter`/`WithFilters` into inherited limit/marker queries and 14 local Body fields. It distinguishes top-level raw name from meta.name and compares raw metadata/timestamps. id is literal id or full order_ref; order_id/secret_id are separate HREF accessors. Whole-page native Order/Meta decoding precedes typed Order results. Common WithName and name Refs are unsupported; ID fetch/delete/wait use the caller's fixed order path. See [order listing](orders/listing/README.md) for metadata comparison, both formatters, repeated queries, pinned-source checks and model boundaries.

`Containers.Resources.List/All` classifies `resource.WithFilter`/`WithFilters` into inherited limit/marker queries and ten local Body fields. Semantic name is local, unlike WithName's server hint. Timestamps, references and nested arrays are compared against original rows; id is literal id or full container_ref, while container_id is a separate HREF accessor. Whole-page native decoding precedes typed Container results. See [container listing](containers/listing/README.md) for raw name/offset extensions, repeated queries, arrays, source checks and model boundaries.

`Secrets.Resources.List/All` classifies Python names into 12 server queries or 12 local Body fields. algorithm maps to alg; canonical input wins when both occur in a bulk option. created_at/updated_at/expires_at compare raw timestamps, id compares literal id or full secret_ref, and secret_id uses a separate HREF accessor. Raw-row comparison follows whole-page native decoding and returns typed Secret. See [secret listing](secrets/listing/README.md) for repeated queries, snapshots, collisions, local caps, model boundaries and source checks.

`Secrets.FindIdentity(ctx, identity, options...)` first attempts metadata/conditional-payload fetch for a safe ID, then searches the full metadata inventory by exact ID/name with a name hint after default HTTP400/403/404. List results get no extra payload fetch. Select missing/fallback policy with `resource.WithIdentityFindIgnoreMissing(false)` and `WithIdentityFindFallback`. Raw query, details, all-projects and extra-specs options are unsupported. Raw response id/secret_ref are comparison inputs, never followed as request paths. See [secret identity finding](secrets/finding/README.md) for nullable IDs, duplicates, offsets, fixed service configuration and Python default-status differences. Native `Secrets.Resources` remains the metadata collection.

`Secrets.GetPayload(ctx, secretID)` returns the full payload `[]byte` and closes the native response body. Accept defaults to text/plain and can be changed through concrete `GetPayloadOpts`. See [payload reads](secrets/payload.md) for native errors, headers and replacing Download with bytes.

`Secrets.Fetch(ctx, resource.ID(secretID))` gets metadata, then fetches payload at the original ID only if a content type is selected. Selection defaults to metadata content_types.default; `WithFetchContentType` overrides it and `WithFetchPayload(false)` requests metadata only. Only exact text/plain becomes UTF-8 text; other types remain bytes. Both HTTP bodies/headers/statuses and request IDs stay distinct, and metadata survives later payload failure. Native `Secrets.Get`/`GetPayload` remain separate calls. See [secrets](secrets/README.md) for content type, fixed paths, options, errors and seeded Python Resource differences.

`Containers.Fetch(ctx, resource.ID(id))` and `Orders.Fetch(ctx, resource.ID(id))` return owned metadata GET results. Original request ID, declared attribute view and actual Wire/HTTP receipt remain distinct; foreign response references are not followed. See [metadata fetch](metadata-fetch.md) for nullable arrays, arbitrary order meta, IDs and errors.

`Containers.CreateRecord`, `Orders.CreateRecord` and `Secrets.CreateRecord` merge creation inputs with the actual POST response into a Resource view. `WithCreateRecordAttributes`/`WithCreateRecordAttribute` represent omitted/null/empty values and aliases; the SDK handles snapshots, flat bodies and fixed paths. Actual Wire/HTTP receipt stays separate from inputs; creation triggers no automatic GET, payload GET or wait. See [metadata creation](metadata-create.md).

`Containers.Remove`, `Orders.Remove`, `Secrets.Remove` and default `Resources.Delete` use owned DELETE, retaining default ignore404 and `resource.WithMissingError()`. Accepted bodies are not interpreted; read/Close/source/context failures preserve actual HTTP evidence. Native `Delete(ctx, string)` retains 202/204 and strict errors. See [metadata deletion](metadata-delete.md) for IDs/names, statuses, partial errors and Python mapping.

SDK-owned `SecretStores` and `Quotas` complement native Barbican APIs. `SecretStores.List/All`, `GetGlobalDefault` and `GetPreferred` provide inventory and fixed-selector reads without fallback, CRUD or waits. `Quotas.Get` reads authenticated-project effective quota; `Quotas.InProject(ctx, resource.ID(projectID))` fixes a project for Get/Update/Delete. Update replaces configuration with PUT204; Delete resets overrides with DELETE204; neither refetches automatically. Actual empty acknowledgement, headers/status are distinct from Python seeded Resource. `secretstores.WithListFilter`/`WithListFilters` classifies nine server queries and five local attributes with raw comparison/caps. See [secret stores](secretstores/README.md) and [quotas](quotas/README.md) for markers, nullable responses, integer inputs, defaults and remaining Resource/cache contracts. Use `service.Quotas.Get(ctx)` for current-project quota without a project ID, preserving raw values and actual HTTP error evidence.

`Secrets.FindRecord` owns metadata/required-payload fetch, default missing handling and list fallback. See [secret finding](secret-find-python.md) for strict HTTP defaults, bytes/text and pagination error evidence.

Concrete `SecretConsumers.CreateRecord/DeleteRecord/ListRecords` options handle nullable attributes, default missing behaviour and local filters while separating raw HTTP from seeded Resource. See [consumer comparison](secret-consumers-python.md) for fixed parent secret, offset paging and physical errors.

`SecretConsumers.InSecret(ctx, resource.ID(secretID))` creates/deletes/lists associations for a fixed secret. Associations use service/resource_type/resource_id, without a separate consumer ID. Create/Delete return actual HTTP200 secret responses; listing follows advertised offset next links. See [secret consumers](secretconsumers/README.md) for all three proxy operations, delete404 defaults, fixed parents, responses and seeded Python Resource differences.

## Go usage

```go
// Inside a function with context.Context ctx and *openstack.Connection conn.
service, err := conn.KeyManagerV1(ctx)
if err != nil { return err }
for value, err := range service.Secrets.Resources.List(ctx) {
    if err != nil { return err }
    fmt.Println(value)
}
value, err := service.Secrets.Find(ctx, resource.Name("example"))
if err != nil { return err }
_ = value
```

Examples use standard-library `fmt` and `github.com/JSYoo5B/go-openstacksdk/resource`. Find treats missing resources as errors by default; `resource.WithIgnoreMissing()` returns `nil, nil`. Delete ignores missing resources by default.

## Resources and common policies

| Service field | API package | Common policies and scope |
|---|---|---|
| `Acls` | [acls](acls/api_generated.go) | API operations; no common Collection policies |
| `Containers` | [containers](containers/api_generated.go) | `Resources`: ID reads, lists, name lookup, deletion/deletion waits, status waits |
| `Orders` | [orders](orders/api_generated.go) | `Resources`: ID reads, lists, deletion/deletion waits, status waits |
| `Quotas` | [quotas](quotas/api.go) | `Get(ctx)`: authenticated-project effective quota; `InProject(ctx, ID)`: Get/replacement Update/override Delete; no list/Find/Wait |
| `SecretACLs` | [secretacls](secretacls/api.go) | `InSecret(ctx, ref)`: Python secret ACL Get, PUT Set/Update, ignore-missing Delete; absent attributes cause no HTTP; no Resources/list/Find/Wait |
| `SecretConsumers` | [secretconsumers](secretconsumers/api.go) | `InSecret(ctx, ref)`: association Create/Delete and offset List/All; actual secret responses; no consumer ID/Resources/Find/Wait |
| `Secrets` | [secrets](secrets/api_generated.go) | `Resources`: ID reads, lists, name lookup, deletion/deletion waits, status waits |
| `SecretStores` | [secretstores](secretstores/api.go) | `List/All`, `GetGlobalDefault`, `GetPreferred`: lists and two fixed reads; no Resources/CRUD/Find/Wait |
| `Waits` | [waits](waits/README.md) | API operations; no common Collection policies |

Common Collections provide exact name lookup, duplicate-name errors, pagination, context cancellation, and preserved HTTP errors. Wait returns `ErrUnsupported` for resources without status support.

Native-pager `Resources.List/All` and parent-scope `List/All` accept `resource.WithMaxItems(n)` and `resource.WithPaginated(false)` to cap raw rows or consume only the first page. Caps apply before local name/status and Trove user-host filters. Zero is unlimited; negative values fail during lazy iteration before HTTP. Native routes do not send caps as wire limit hints and preserve explicit page sizes, queries, and headers. Full-page extraction may still fail on malformed rows beyond the cap. Existing operation-specific options remain available on native typed List; common consumption options belong to Collections/scopes. See [service list comparisons](../../docs/listing.md) for actual bindings and continuation policies.

## Mutation requests

Pass concrete options to resource Create/Update APIs. Use typed options for standard fields and With...Field for extension fields. Queries and headers use the operation's With... functions. Standard-field/header overrides and unsupported extension mechanisms are rejected before requests. The SDK implements request-builder interfaces.

Operations requiring parents use [scope objects](../../docs/scoped-resources.md), whose Create/Update methods accept the same concrete options. This API reference does not imply support for response tracking or every composite Python cloud operation.
